newsitem.title: USA: Enron extends Cajun low price offer.
newsitem.headline: Enron extends Cajun low price offer.

text.p: Enron Capital & Trade Resources said it is offering to extend, at Cajun members options, a low-rate price option in its Cajun Electric Power Cooperative Inc bankruptcy proposal for 10 years beyond the 15 year primary term of the proposal.
The price guarantee and extension are anticipated to cap the rate Cajun members will pay for electricity at $0.04 per kilowatt hour for up to 25 years, the Enron Corp unit said.
Company officials were not immediately available to provide details on Enron's offer to the Louisiana Public Service Commission.
Southwestern Electric Power spokesman Peter Main said the Enron filing is in response to a mid-December request from the Louisiana Commission.

At that time, the commission noted two of the pending Cajun offers -- from Central and South West Corp and Entergy Corp, and from Southern Co, Northern States Power Co and Zeigler Coal Holding Co -- included 25 year price caps, making them hard to compare with Enron's 15 year cap.

The spokesman for Southwestern, the Central and South West unit involved in the company's Cajun offer, said the bankruptcy confirmation hearing was adjourned to March 10 after the bankruptcy judge dismissed the members committee's bankruptcy attorney at the request of one of the member coops.
Main said the judge has called a status conference for February 24 when it will be decided whether to proceed with the March 10 hearing. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
